title: Only Fire and Sea Can Look at Each Other...
text:
Only fire and sea can look at each other

without end. Not even the sky with its clouds.

Only your face, only the sea and fire.

The flames, and the waves, and your eyes.

You will be of fire and sea, dark eyes.

Of wave and flame you will be, black hair.

You will know the outcome of the bonfire.

And you will know the secret of the foam.

Crowned in blue like the wave.

Keen and sidereal like the flame.

Only your face endlessly.

Like fire and sea. Like death.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's incantatory repetition of fire, sea, face, and death.

title: You Are Like the High and Slender Light...
text:
You are like the high and slender light.

Like the wind you are clear without knowing it.

Your bearing wavers like the afternoon

softly leaning over the world.


You are made of forgotten dreams

and I forget you suddenly, as one forgets a dream;

my heart seeks you as smoke

seeks the height and dies toward it.


Like a warm flower the day carries you

fastened between its lips. You are tall,

blue, slender, and straight as a whistle.

I remember you suddenly as one remembers a dream.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the beloved as light, wind, smoke, flower, and remembered dream.

title: Theme of Dream and Life
text:
Dream me,

        dream me, half-open lips.

Sleeping mouth, you who smile, dream me.


        Down through dream, beautiful water, pure limbs,

beneath the moon, slender one,

        dream me.

Awake,

        dream me as you breathe,

without knowing it, forgotten, brown skin;

dream me

        love, love, with winter

like a purple flower upon the shoulder.

Oh slender

        garden whose slender waist

I have held for so long;

oh flame of

        black eyes, my love;

oh course of water among dreams.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the repeated plea to be dreamed and the catalog's indented lyric movement.

title: The Most Beautiful Head Was Falling...
text:
The most beautiful head was falling

toward the side of dreams; summer

was a jasmine without borders, and in her hand

the day floated like a blue handkerchief.


And her mouth suddenly was falling

toward the side of kisses; summer

held her in the palm of its hand,

made of love, oh, what melancholy!


Along the shores of this love a river crossed;

over this love there was a palm tree:

water of time and sky-poetry.


And the river carried away everything of mine;

the hand and the summer and my palm tree

of poetry. Oh, what melancholy!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Carranza's dreamward movement and the refrain of melancholy as the river carries everything away.
